overview: Umbrella review of published reviews of point-of-care lactate at emergency department triage in adults with suspected sepsis, with outcomes chosen for a triage decision, a citation matrix to handle overlap, and a confidence rating for each review; October 2026 to March 2027.
population: Reviews (with a stated search and inclusion criteria) of adults with suspected sepsis or suspected infection in emergency departments that report lactate accuracy or outcomes by lactate; reviews limited to intensive care or children are excluded.
exposure: Lactate measured at or near triage, point-of-care or laboratory, with sample type recorded; thresholds of 2 and 4 mmol/L extracted where reported.
procedures: The librarian searches four databases and two registers of review protocols. Two reviewers (the clinical fellow and the investigator) screen titles, abstracts and full texts, extract review characteristics, outcomes, thresholds, sample types and included primary studies, and rate each review with a standard critical appraisal checklist. A citation matrix of primary studies gives the corrected covered area; where reviews overlap, the most recent review of adequate confidence is used for each outcome and threshold. Results are derived at the department's prevalence where reviews report sensitivity and specificity.

outcomes.name: False reassurance
outcomes.measure: Proportion of patients with lactate below the threshold who have sepsis with organ dysfunction (one minus negative predictive value), as reported or derived at local prevalence
outcomes.why: The error that would harm patients if a normal value lowered priority; the investigator's main concern.

outcomes.name: Accuracy at 2 and 4 mmol/L
outcomes.measure: Sensitivity and specificity for sepsis with organ dysfunction and for in-hospital death, as pooled by each review, kept separate by outcome
outcomes.why: Shows the threshold trade-off behind any rule.

outcomes.name: False alarms
outcomes.measure: Proportion of patients with a raised lactate who do not have sepsis with organ dysfunction (one minus positive predictive value) at local prevalence, and reported effects on resuscitation-area use
outcomes.why: The cost of a triage rule to other patients through crowding and delay.

outcomes.name: Overlap of primary studies
outcomes.measure: Corrected covered area from the citation matrix, overall and by outcome
outcomes.why: Prevents counting the same evidence twice.

outcomes.name: Confidence in each review
outcomes.measure: Rating from the critical appraisal checklist (high, moderate, low, critically low)
outcomes.why: Conclusions must carry the confidence of the reviews they rest on.

feasibility: Eight fellow hours a week over six months, the librarian's search under LIB-2026-311, and no translation budget; reviews in other languages are placed in the matrix from abstracts and tables where possible and listed.
biasMitigation: Two independent reviewers for selection, extraction and confidence ratings
Citation matrix to prevent double counting
Outcomes for sepsis with organ dysfunction and for death kept separate
Sample type and threshold recorded for every estimate

biasFlags.label: Overlapping reviews
biasFlags.note: Handled by the citation matrix and one review per outcome and threshold.

biasFlags.label: Spectrum bias in primary studies
biasFlags.note: Studies that tested only unwell patients overstate sensitivity; recorded for each review.

biasFlags.label: Language restriction
biasFlags.note: No translation budget; reviews in other languages listed and placed where possible.

flags: False reassurance is primary; accuracy is secondary; false alarms are a balancing outcome, which is unusual for an accuracy question but matches the triage decision
parsimony.simplestPath: One primary triage error, one accuracy table, one balancing error, a citation matrix and confidence ratings.

theoreticalFramework: None; GRADE-style reasoning is applied to the reviews' conclusions through the confidence ratings.
summary: Umbrella review with false reassurance as the primary outcome, accuracy as secondary, false alarms as balancing, and overlap and confidence as process measures.
